title: Input and output examples
responsibility: Shows documented uses beside expected outcomes, or recorded calls beside observed results.

inputs.name: EntityCases.document
inputs.description: Optional recorded document passed with unit to artifactCases when examples is undefined, to produce observed rows or a gap. In the non-gap recorded view, it appears in the expandable full-values disclosure.

inputs.name: EntityCases.examples
inputs.description: Optional array of UsageExample values; defining it selects documented mode, and an empty array shows the no-documented-examples message. It takes precedence over document and its entries provide expected rows.

inputs.name: EntityCases.unit
inputs.description: Optional unit identifier passed with document to artifactCases only when examples is undefined. It defaults to undefined (omitted), so examples mode does not use it.

inputs.name: EntityCases.callable
inputs.description: Controls whether the observed note says the result was not a direct call of the function. Defaults to true and matters only for recorded cases whose source is not invocations.

outputs.name: EntityCases
outputs.description: Renders documented examples as expected outcomes, recorded artifact cases as observed results, or a gap message when the source reports a gap; failed cases are marked as errors. Outside the gap state, an expandable disclosure shows the full selected examples or document, while the component presents recorded values rather than invoking the represented function.

errors.name: TypeError
errors.description: Expanding the full-values disclosure calls JSON.stringify, which throws for BigInt values or circular structures.

errors.name: RangeError
errors.description: Expanding the full-values disclosure can raise a range error when deeply nested values exhaust the JSON serializer recursion stack.

errors.name: Value access or serialization callback error
errors.description: Reading row values or serializing the selected document or examples can invoke supplied getters, proxy traps, or toJSON methods; their thrown errors propagate.
